Terms, privacy, and supportPlain terms, a privacy page, and a support page with one public address, the person who runs this server, shared with Simple Hack.

The terms cover acceptable use (including terrorism, hate, self-harm, sexual services, search spam, and misinformation such as dangerous health claims, misleading voters, and manipulated media; satire, parody, and opinion are fine), named regulated goods, selling from a site (allowed; payment goes through a provider and the site owner is the seller), what the service and saved data are not for, children's and special-category data, trademark and likeness requests, legal-request channels, what evidence is kept, and a security-report line. Intimate images are removed within 48 hours of a valid request. Appeals are open for 30 days and a person reads each one and gives one answer. Adverse changes get 14 days' notice. "description": "Optional. Every site already lives at its own address `https://\u003csite\u003e.\u003chandle\u003e.golden-host.invalid/`, with sign-in and private lists. This gives it a nicer address; the site moves there and its old address redirects. A free address: send `{\"domain\": \"\u003cname\u003e.golden-host.invalid\"}` (one DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end, up to 63 characters). It is active at once with no DNS step — the answer has `status: active` and `verified_at`, and no `dns`. First come, first served: 409 domain_taken if another site holds it or it is already someone's handle (handles and free names share one namespace); reserved names (www, sites, api, admin, mail, cname and the platform's own hosts) get 400 name_reserved; anything else malformed gets 400 invalid_name. Once claimed it behaves exactly like a custom domain: the site is served at its root with a same-origin /v1 API and visitor sign-in, its person-address URL 302s there, and private collections take submissions there. A site has one own address: claiming one replaces a custom domain and vice versa. A free name the site lets go (switching, DELETE, or deleting the site) stays with it: it redirects to the site's current address and nobody else can claim it. A custom domain: bind ONE domain to the site (status starts as `pending`). Returns the two DNS records the owner must create: `dns` (CNAME for a subdomain, A for an apex) and `dns_txt`, the ownership record (TXT `_simple-host.\u003cdomain\u003e` holding this site's token), which proves the domain is theirs and must stay in place. Nothing is verified or certified without it. A name another site on this server already serves is refused by the certificate issuer (failed, \"already served here\"). Once both records are seen, its certificate is requested automatically (at most 5 new domain certificates per account per day) (`certificate_status`: pending → issuing → live, or failed with the reason in `last_error`, retried) and the domain is served at its root, usually within minutes. If the site already has a working own address (a free name or an earlier domain), it keeps serving there (`previous_domain`) until the new domain is verified; then the old address redirects to it. Binding the site's current working domain again changes nothing; binding its `previous_domain` drops the pending one. Until first verified, a binding is provisional: another site can take it over until it has passed its ownership proof, and it expires 24 hours after binding unless DNS already points here. A verified domain stays exclusive while it works; if it fails every check for 24 hours the owner is emailed, and after 72 hours it is disconnected (the site's own address serves again) and can be connected afresh, with the TXT record, by whoever holds it; while it is being released, binding it answers 409 domain_releasing. The platform's own zones (including event domains such as simple-hack.app) are refused (400 invalid_domain). A domain under the account's own address family may be connected; the exact domain wins. `*.\u003cdomain\u003e` answers 400 use_address_family (see POST /v1/me/address-families). Owner only (API key).\n\nwww and the bare domain (where the certificate issuer runs, as on golden-host.invalid; absent elsewhere): binding `example.com` also sets up `www.example.com` (and binding `www.example.com` sets up `example.com`) as a redirect-only host that forwards (301) to the name chosen. The answer names it (`partner_domain`) with the record it needs (`dns_partner`); the TXT record on the chosen name covers both. It goes on the same certificate only if it points here and no other site on this server answers it; otherwise the chosen name goes live alone and `partner_status` is `not_set_up` with `partner_note` saying why.",

"description": "The Add photos page at /photos prepares images on the person's device. Upload 1 to 30 WebP or JPEG files as repeated photos multipart parts. The endpoint accepts X-API-Key, including the dashboard's stored owner key and account-wide deploy-only keys (not site-scoped), with the normal deploy permissions and rate limit. Visitor cookies do not authorize it. Browser origins must match the apex. Default limits are 1,000,000 bytes per photo (PHOTO_MAX_BYTES) and 2048 pixels on the longest side (PHOTO_MAX_DIMENSION). The server validates headers and container structure without decoding pixels or re-encoding. This is header-only validation, not a full decode of the compressed image. JPEG allows JFIF APP0, ICC_PROFILE APP2 (16 KB total), and Adobe APP14; comments and other APP markers are refused. WebP ICCP is limited to 16 KB; EXIF, XMP, animation, unknown chunks and trailing data are refused. ICC contents are not inspected; browser canvas output carries no profile or a standard profile. Signed-in and photo-token saves share PHOTO_MAX_CONCURRENT slots (default 3), acquired before body reads. Both entry points set a body-read deadline of 60 seconds (PHOTO_BODY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) on the real response writer; unsupported writers continue normally. Full capacity returns 429 with error \"Busy, try again in a moment\" and Retry-After of 2 seconds, without queueing. Filenames must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,59}\\.(webp|jpg)$ and the extension must match the contents. Files go under images/, with -2, -3, and further suffixes for collisions. Every other live file is kept. After an uncertain response, resend the batch with X-Photo-Reconcile: 1. This only checks for distinct live files with matching names (including collision suffixes) and identical bytes. A full match returns the current version and reconciled: true; it confirms presence, not which request wrote the files. A missing match returns 409 photo_save_uncertain. Checks never create a version. Ordinary saves create one normal published version, with normal file quotas and retention. Hosted and small-box Simple Host only; Simple Hack returns 404.",

Simple Hack answers with read, write, write_mode and site_passcode only.",

"description": "Kind is immutable. Simple Host: set preset (public, inbox, wall, comments, records, personal, board, private; default private) with optional single-action overrides read, add, edit, delete, or preset custom with all four. Each action takes nobody, owner, own, signed-in or anyone; add also takes checked (anyone who passes the Cloudflare Turnstile spam check: the comments preset, read anyone / add checked / edit owner / delete owner). The server refuses (400 invalid_access, with rule) edit or delete anyone (anonymous_change), add own (add_own), own anywhere with add anyone or checked (own_needs_sign_in), checked on read, edit or delete (checked_add_only), and edit or delete wider than read (change_wider_than_read). checked is refused on files resources, and with 400 spam_check_unavailable on a server without TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and a secret (Simple Hack included). approve_first (SQLite, needs a checked add) holds posts added through the check: the server adds approved_at TEXT to those tables (rows already there count as approved), visitors see and reach only rows with approved_at set, and the owner approves with UPDATE ... SET approved_at = datetime('now'). Omit approve_first to keep it. SQLite: the preset is the database default; tables sets a preset per table (omit to keep the current table presets, {} to clear). Tables whose preset uses own or lets visitors add get the server-owned visitor_id TEXT column and index. The older read, write and write_mode are still accepted and translated (write anyone with full is refused as anonymous_change; omitting write_mode on update keeps the mode); do not mix them with preset fields. Switching a legacy SQLite database pages wrote with SQL to a preset that uses own needs empty tables (visitor_id_required). Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. Simple Hack accepts only read and write (anyone, signed-in, owner) with full mode, as before presets. With STORAGE_RULES=on, SQLite and SQLite-stored KV resources also accept rules (StoragePolicySet), without preset fields. A rules save on a Postgres KV namespace returns 400 rules_unavailable. Rules are unavailable on file buckets (400 invalid_rules). A body or table rules field with the flag off returns 400 rules_unavailable. Bodies over 256 KiB return 400 invalid_rules with clause size. Null rules are treated as absent; an empty policies array denies visitors. For SQLite, table rules override the default set; omit tables to keep overrides, or send tables {} to clear them. When moving from per-table presets, send rules for every override or tables {}. Preset fields and rules on the same body or table entry return 400 invalid_rules. A rules resource saved back to presets with table overrides requires explicit tables (otherwise 409 tables_present). A passcode-only save on a rules resource preserves rules. Rules responses omit preset fields and carry rules, rules_status and rules_errors. Preset responses remain unchanged with the flag off; with it on they also carry rules_status preset.",

"description": "Optional. Every site already lives at its own address `https://\u003csite\u003e.\u003chandle\u003e.golden-host.invalid/`, with sign-in and private lists. This gives it a nicer address; the site moves there and its old address redirects. A free address: send `{\"domain\": \"\u003cname\u003e.golden-host.invalid\"}` (one DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end, up to 63 characters). It is active at once with no DNS step — the answer has `status: active` and `verified_at`, and no `dns`. First come, first served: 409 domain_taken if another site holds it or it is already someone's handle (handles and free names share one namespace); reserved names (www, sites, api, admin, mail, cname and the platform's own hosts) get 400 name_reserved; anything else malformed gets 400 invalid_name. Once claimed it behaves exactly like a custom domain: the site is served at its root with a same-origin /v1 API and visitor sign-in, its person-address URL 302s there, and private collections take submissions there. A site has one own address: claiming one replaces a custom domain and vice versa. A free name the site lets go (switching, DELETE, or deleting the site) stays with it: it redirects to the site's current address and nobody else can claim it. A custom domain: bind ONE domain to the site (status starts as `pending`). Returns the two DNS records the owner must create: `dns` (CNAME for a subdomain, A for an apex) and `dns_txt`, the ownership record (TXT `_simple-host.\u003cdomain\u003e` holding this site's token), which proves the domain is theirs and must stay in place. Nothing is verified or certified without it. A name another site on this server already serves is refused by the certificate issuer (failed, \"already served here\"). Once both records are seen, its certificate is requested automatically (at most 5 new domain certificates per account per day) (`certificate_status`: pending → issuing → live, or failed with the reason in `last_error`, retried) and the domain is served at its root, usually within minutes. If the site already has a working own address (a free name or an earlier domain), it keeps serving there (`previous_domain`) until the new domain is verified; then the old address redirects to it. Binding the site's current working domain again changes nothing; binding its `previous_domain` drops the pending one. Until first verified, a binding is provisional: another site can take it over until it has passed its ownership proof, and it expires 24 hours after binding unless DNS already points here. A verified domain stays exclusive while it works; if it fails every check for 24 hours the owner is emailed, and after 72 hours it is disconnected (the site's own address serves again) and can be connected afresh, with the TXT record, by whoever holds it; while it is being released, binding it answers 409 domain_releasing. The platform's own zones are refused (400 invalid_domain). A domain under the account's own address family may be connected; the exact domain wins. `*.\u003cdomain\u003e` answers 400 use_address_family (see POST /v1/me/address-families). Owner only (API key).\n\nwww and the bare domain (where the certificate issuer runs, as on golden-host.invalid; absent elsewhere): binding `example.com` also sets up `www.example.com` (and binding `www.example.com` sets up `example.com`) as a redirect-only host that forwards (301) to the name chosen. The answer names it (`partner_domain`) with the record it needs (`dns_partner`); the TXT record on the chosen name covers both. It goes on the same certificate only if it points here and no other site on this server answers it; otherwise the chosen name goes live alone and `partner_status` is `not_set_up` with `partner_note` saying why.",

"description": "The Add photos page at /photos prepares images on the person's device. Upload 1 to 30 WebP or JPEG files as repeated photos multipart parts. Visitor cookies do not authorize it. Browser origins must match the apex. Default limits are 1,000,000 bytes per photo (PHOTO_MAX_BYTES) and 2048 pixels on the longest side (PHOTO_MAX_DIMENSION). The server validates headers and container structure without decoding pixels or re-encoding. This is header-only validation, not a full decode of the compressed image. JPEG allows JFIF APP0, ICC_PROFILE APP2 (16 KB total), and Adobe APP14; comments and other APP markers are refused. WebP ICCP is limited to 16 KB; EXIF, XMP, animation, unknown chunks and trailing data are refused. ICC contents are not inspected; browser canvas output carries no profile or a standard profile. Signed-in and photo-token saves share PHOTO_MAX_CONCURRENT slots (default 3), acquired before body reads. Both entry points set a body-read deadline of 60 seconds (PHOTO_BODY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) on the real response writer; unsupported writers continue normally. Full capacity returns 429 with error \"Busy, try again in a moment\" and Retry-After of 2 seconds, without queueing. Filenames must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,59}\\.(webp|jpg)$ and the extension must match the contents. Files go under images/, with -2, -3, and further suffixes for collisions. Every other live file is kept. After an uncertain response, resend the batch with X-Photo-Reconcile: 1. This only checks for distinct live files with matching names (including collision suffixes) and identical bytes. A full match returns the current version and reconciled: true; it confirms presence, not which request wrote the files. A missing match returns 409 photo_save_uncertain. Checks never create a version. Ordinary saves create one normal published version, with normal file quotas and retention. Hosted and small-box Simple Host only.",

"description": "On Simple Host each resource carries preset (public, inbox, wall, comments, records, personal, board, private, custom with based_on, or legacy), access {read,add,edit,delete}, tables (SQLite, per-table preset and access), approve_first (SQLite), and the older read, write and write_mode whenever the matrix can be expressed in them. legacy marks a resource saved before presets that keeps its old rules until the owner saves a policy on it.",

"description": "Kind is immutable. Simple Host: set preset (public, inbox, wall, comments, records, personal, board, private; default private) with optional single-action overrides read, add, edit, delete, or preset custom with all four. Each action takes nobody, owner, own, signed-in or anyone; add also takes checked (anyone who passes the Cloudflare Turnstile spam check: the comments preset, read anyone / add checked / edit owner / delete owner). The server refuses (400 invalid_access, with rule) edit or delete anyone (anonymous_change), add own (add_own), own anywhere with add anyone or checked (own_needs_sign_in), checked on read, edit or delete (checked_add_only), and edit or delete wider than read (change_wider_than_read). checked is refused on files resources, and with 400 spam_check_unavailable on a server without TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and a secret. approve_first (SQLite, needs a checked add) holds posts added through the check: the server adds approved_at TEXT to those tables (rows already there count as approved), visitors see and reach only rows with approved_at set, and the owner approves with UPDATE ... SET approved_at = datetime('now'). Omit approve_first to keep it. SQLite: the preset is the database default; tables sets a preset per table (omit to keep the current table presets, {} to clear). Tables whose preset uses own or lets visitors add get the server-owned visitor_id TEXT column and index. The older read, write and write_mode are still accepted and translated (write anyone with full is refused as anonymous_change; omitting write_mode on update keeps the mode); do not mix them with preset fields. Switching a legacy SQLite database pages wrote with SQL to a preset that uses own needs empty tables (visitor_id_required). Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. With STORAGE_RULES=on, SQLite and SQLite-stored KV resources also accept rules (StoragePolicySet), without preset fields. A rules save on a Postgres KV namespace returns 400 rules_unavailable. Rules are unavailable on file buckets (400 invalid_rules). A body or table rules field with the flag off returns 400 rules_unavailable. Bodies over 256 KiB return 400 invalid_rules with clause size. Null rules are treated as absent; an empty policies array denies visitors. For SQLite, table rules override the default set; omit tables to keep overrides, or send tables {} to clear them. When moving from per-table presets, send rules for every override or tables {}. Preset fields and rules on the same body or table entry return 400 invalid_rules. A rules resource saved back to presets with table overrides requires explicit tables (otherwise 409 tables_present). A passcode-only save on a rules resource preserves rules. Rules responses omit preset fields and carry rules, rules_status and rules_errors. Preset responses remain unchanged with the flag off; with it on they also carry rules_status preset.",

"description": "Checked against the table's add value. One JSON object of real column names and scalar values. Visitor visitor_id, created_at and updated_at are ignored; visitor_id is filled from the site session and created_at with UTC time when the columns exist. | Optional. Every site already lives at its own address `https://<site>.<handle>.golden-host.invalid/`, with sign-in and private lists. This gives it a nicer address; the site moves there and its old address redirects. A free address: send `{"domain": "<name>.golden-host.invalid"}` (one DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end, up to 63 characters). It is active at once with no DNS step — the answer has `status: active` and `verified_at`, and no `dns`. First come, first served: 409 domain_taken if another site holds it or it is already someone's handle (handles and free names share one namespace); reserved names (www, sites, api, admin, mail, cname and the platform's own hosts) get 400 name_reserved; anything else malformed gets 400 invalid_name. Once claimed it behaves exactly like a custom domain: the site is served at its root with a same-origin /v1 API and visitor sign-in, its person-address URL 302s there, and private collections take submissions there. A site has one own address: claiming one replaces a custom domain and vice versa. A free name the site lets go (switching, DELETE, or deleting the site) stays with it: it redirects to the site's current address and nobody else can claim it. A custom domain: bind ONE domain to the site (status starts as `pending`). Returns the two DNS records the owner must create: `dns` (CNAME for a subdomain, A for an apex) and `dns_txt`, the ownership record (TXT `_simple-host.<domain>` holding this site's token), which proves the domain is theirs and must stay in place. Nothing is verified or certified without it. A name another site on this server already serves is refused by the certificate issuer (failed, "already served here"). Once both records are seen, its certificate is requested automatically (at most 5 new domain certificates per account per day) (`certificate_status`: pending → issuing → live, or failed with the reason in `last_error`, retried) and the domain is served at its root, usually within minutes. If the site already has a working own address (a free name or an earlier domain), it keeps serving there (`previous_domain`) until the new domain is verified; then the old address redirects to it. Binding the site's current working domain again changes nothing; binding its `previous_domain` drops the pending one. Until first verified, a binding is provisional: another site can take it over until it has passed its ownership proof, and it expires 24 hours after binding unless DNS already points here. A verified domain stays exclusive while it works; if it fails every check for 24 hours the owner is emailed, and after 72 hours it is disconnected (the site's own address serves again) and can be connected afresh, with the TXT record, by whoever holds it; while it is being released, binding it answers 409 domain_releasing. The platform's own zones (including event domains such as simple-hack.app) are refused (400 invalid_domain). A domain under the account's own address family may be connected; the exact domain wins. `*.<domain>` answers 400 use_address_family (see POST /v1/me/address-families). Owner only (API key).

"description": "The Add photos page at /photos prepares images on the person's device. Upload 1 to 30 WebP or JPEG files as repeated photos multipart parts. The endpoint accepts X-API-Key, including the dashboard's stored owner key and account-wide deploy-only keys (not site-scoped), with the normal deploy permissions and rate limit. Visitor cookies do not authorize it. Browser origins must match the apex. Default limits are 1,000,000 bytes per photo (PHOTO_MAX_BYTES) and 2048 pixels on the longest side (PHOTO_MAX_DIMENSION). The server validates headers and container structure without decoding pixels or re-encoding. This is header-only validation, not a full decode of the compressed image. JPEG allows JFIF APP0, ICC_PROFILE APP2 (16 KB total), and Adobe APP14; comments and other APP markers are refused. WebP ICCP is limited to 16 KB; EXIF, XMP, animation, unknown chunks and trailing data are refused. ICC contents are not inspected; browser canvas output carries no profile or a standard profile. Signed-in and photo-token saves share PHOTO_MAX_CONCURRENT slots (default 3), acquired before body reads. Both entry points set a body-read deadline of 60 seconds (PHOTO_BODY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) on the real response writer; unsupported writers continue normally. Full capacity returns 429 with error \"Busy, try again in a moment\" and Retry-After of 2 seconds, without queueing. Filenames must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,59}\\.(webp|jpg)$ and the extension must match the contents. Files go under images/, with -2, -3, and further suffixes for collisions. Every other live file is kept. After an uncertain response, resend the batch with X-Photo-Reconcile: 1. This only checks for distinct live files with matching names (including collision suffixes) and identical bytes. A full match returns the current version and reconciled: true; it confirms presence, not which request wrote the files. A missing match returns 409 photo_save_uncertain. Checks never create a version. Ordinary saves create one normal published version, with normal file quotas and retention. Hosted and small-box Simple Host only; Simple Hack returns 404.",

Simple Hack answers with read, write, write_mode and site_passcode only.",

"description": "Kind is immutable. Simple Host: set preset (public, inbox, wall, comments, records, personal, board, private; default private) with optional single-action overrides read, add, edit, delete, or preset custom with all four. Each action takes nobody, owner, own, signed-in or anyone; add also takes checked (anyone who passes the Cloudflare Turnstile spam check: the comments preset, read anyone / add checked / edit owner / delete owner). The server refuses (400 invalid_access, with rule) edit or delete anyone (anonymous_change), add own (add_own), own anywhere with add anyone or checked (own_needs_sign_in), checked on read, edit or delete (checked_add_only), and edit or delete wider than read (change_wider_than_read). checked is refused on files resources, and with 400 spam_check_unavailable on a server without TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and a secret (Simple Hack included). approve_first (SQLite, needs a checked add) holds posts added through the check: the server adds approved_at TEXT to those tables (rows already there count as approved), visitors see and reach only rows with approved_at set, and the owner approves with UPDATE ... SET approved_at = datetime('now'). Omit approve_first to keep it. SQLite: the preset is the database default; tables sets a preset per table (omit to keep the current table presets, {} to clear). Tables whose preset uses own or lets visitors add get the server-owned visitor_id TEXT column and index. The older read, write and write_mode are still accepted and translated (write anyone with full is refused as anonymous_change; omitting write_mode on update keeps the mode); do not mix them with preset fields. Switching a legacy SQLite database pages wrote with SQL to a preset that uses own needs empty tables (visitor_id_required). Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. Simple Hack accepts only read and write (anyone, signed-in, owner) with full mode, as before presets. With STORAGE_RULES=on, SQLite and SQLite-stored KV resources also accept rules (StoragePolicySet), without preset fields. A rules save on a Postgres KV namespace returns 400 rules_unavailable. Rules are unavailable on file buckets (400 invalid_rules). A body or table rules field with the flag off returns 400 rules_unavailable. Bodies over 256 KiB return 400 invalid_rules with clause size. Null rules are treated as absent; an empty policies array denies visitors. For SQLite, table rules override the default set; omit tables to keep overrides, or send tables {} to clear them. When moving from per-table presets, send rules for every override or tables {}. Preset fields and rules on the same body or table entry return 400 invalid_rules. A rules resource saved back to presets with table overrides requires explicit tables (otherwise 409 tables_present). A passcode-only save on a rules resource preserves rules. Rules responses omit preset fields and carry rules, rules_status and rules_errors. Preset responses remain unchanged with the flag off; with it on they also carry rules_status preset.",

"description": "Checked against the table's add value. One JSON object of real column names and scalar values. Visitor visitor_id, created_at and updated_at are ignored; visitor_id is filled from the site session and created_at with UTC time when the columns exist. Declared SQLite foreign keys must point at a row the visitor may read under the parent table's read value (for own, a row they added), checked inside the insert transaction. Missing and unreadable parents both return 404 invalid_reference; the insert is rolled back. Optional references must be all NULL; partial composite NULLs are refused. A trigger or foreign-key action that writes another table refuses the insert (403). No visitor SQL accepted. Where add is checked (the comments preset), a caller other than the owner sends the one-time Turnstile token in X-SH-Turnstile (auth.js does it on its own); without one 403 spam_check_required, a failed, reused, expired or mismatched one 403 spam_check_failed, Cloudflare unreachable 403 spam_check_unavailable. The token must have been solved in the frame at GET /v1/turnstile/frame for this host and resource. Such a post is at most SPAM_CHECKED_POST_MAX_BYTES (413 post_too_large) with at most SPAM_CHECKED_POST_MAX_LINKS links (400 too_many_links), and RATE_LIMIT_SPAM_CHECKED_IP and RATE_LIMIT_SPAM_CHECKED_SITE apply (429). The same holds for adding a KV key. The query param for (owner, or the owner signed in on the site's own address, only; SIM-358, 2026-11-06, review fixes 2026-11-06) adds this row for one other signed-in visitor instead of the caller, by their visitor_id or the email they signed in with, only on a table whose read is own (403 for_requires_own on any other table, checked on the table's own matrix). It is refused (404 visitor_unknown) if they have never signed in on this site, or (400 visitor_email_ambiguous) if more than one signed-in person currently matches that email; there is no pre-sign-in email binding. The server ignores any visitor_id or written_by the caller sends and sets them itself, visitor_id to that visitor and written_by (added lazily, under the write lock, the first time a table is used this way; 409 written_by_blocked if a trigger or view appears to depend on the table) to owner, otherwise the empty string, which is also written_by's value whenever for is absent, including a plain owner add. A row added this way does not fire record.added to the owner's own subscriptions. Host only, 404 on Simple Hack and event storage.",

If the site already has a working own address (a free name or an earlier domain), it keeps serving there (`previous_domain`) until the new domain is verified; then the old address redirects to it. Binding the site's current working domain again changes nothing; binding its `previous_domain` drops the pending one. Until first verified, a binding is provisional: another site can take it over until it has passed its ownership proof, and it expires 24 hours after binding unless DNS already points here. A verified domain stays exclusive while it works; if it fails every check for 24 hours the owner is emailed, and after 72 hours it is disconnected (the site's own address serves again) and can be connected afresh, with the TXT record, by whoever holds it; while it is being released, binding it answers 409 domain_releasing. removed: On a table whose permissive read alternatives require author or owner with at least one author alternative (for_requires_own otherwise), the owner may add a row for one already-signed-in visitor instead of themselves: POST .../tables/<table>/rows?for=<visitor_id or their email> (auth.js: table().add(values, {for})), or MCP storage_sql_execute with table and values in place of sql and params. Refused 404 visitor_unknown if that person has never signed in on this site, or 400 visitor_email_ambiguous if more than one signed-in person currently matches that email; no pre-sign-in email binding. The row's visitor_id is theirs and a written_by column reads "owner" (otherwise ""), visible on every read; a trigger that rewrites either one as a side effect of the insert is caught and the add rolled back (409 written_by_tampered); it does not fire record.added to the owner's own subscriptions; raw storage_sql_execute refuses a statement naming written_by, including inside a new trigger or view (a positional INSERT naming no column is not caught, by design). GET .../storage/people (SH.storage.people()) is the owner's pick list: people with saved data here or named-viewer status, never everyone who has signed in; storage_visitor_emails also takes emails, resolving each to the reference for takes. Host only: 404 on Simple Hack. get_page_recipe topic people is a worked example (coach and clients).

Create a site private from its first request: create_site with access "specific" and optional viewers ["person@example.com"] in the SAME call. No viewers means only the owner. Never create an open site and then lock it. Default/anyone stays open to anyone with the address. REST JSON POST /v1/sites/<name>/files accepts access and viewers alongside files; archive POST /v1/sites/<name>?access=specific&viewers=a@example.com,b@example.com also accepts repeated viewers=. PUT ?create=1 supports the same options: on an existing site specific requires it already be specific (409 access_differs); anyone never changes existing access; viewers are added only at creation. Plain PUT with access/viewers is 400 invalid_request. Invalid emails: 400 invalid_email; too many: 400 too_many_viewers. Refusals before creation: 409 named_viewers_unavailable (Hack), sign_in_unavailable, named_viewers_need_own_address. Requires the same own address and sign-in setup as existing named viewers.
Tell the person to send the people the site's address and to sign in there with the email they named. Not on Simple Hack.

After building a form, offer entry notifications through MCP Events or a dashboard webhook. Read the [notification reference](https://golden-host.invalid/docs/webhooks/) for signatures, retries, and limits. Simple Hack uses personal team or organiser subscriptions. On Simple Host the same subscription also takes four site events, site.deployed, domain.status_changed, viewer.access_requested, and visitor.signed_up (visitor ID only, never an email, never the owner); Simple Hack and Enterprise keep the three record events, and Enterprise needs a separate port for the site events. On Simple Host, Web Push is a third notification kind on the same subscription (SIM-360, behind the account allowlist WEB_PUSH_ACCOUNTS, off until the owner enables it): the owner subscribes a browser device from the dashboard or `SH.push.subscribe()`, and a signed-in visitor may subscribe their own device too, site-wide or to one optional resource, to be told when the owner adds or edits their row. Not yet on Simple Hack or Enterprise.

Simple Hack judging: rubric edits preserve existing criterion IDs and scores. Confirm reported score deletions before retrying with confirm_score_deletion. Automatic assignments include organisers only with include_organisers=true. Scoring opens at Judging, which locks mode, judges per team, rubric and assignments and generates Automatic assignments; returning to Entries closed pauses scoring and unlocks setup.

Simple Hack announcements support [label](https://...), **bold**, - bullets and line breaks; only http/https links. A Zoom/Meet/Teams/YouTube address alone on a line becomes a card. GET and the public feed carry safe body_html and pinned, pinned first. POST accepts pinned; PUT accepts pinned alone to pin/unpin, replacing the previous pin. POST /v1/hack/events/{slug}/announcements/preview is an organiser-only REST preview that stores nothing. MCP hack_post_announcement and hack_edit_announcement accept body.pinned; hack_get_announcements returns body_html and pinned.

Simple Hack organisers can PUT or DELETE /v1/hack/events/{slug}/announcements/{announcement}; Editing does not send a new email. Entry PUT accepts updated_at and returns 409 entry_changed with the current entry on a stale save.

Simple Hack website uploads: signed-in participants can PUT a zip or tar.gz to /v1/hack/events/{slug}/site?create=1 without a team key. Organisers use PUT /v1/hack/events/{slug}/website?create=1, including in draft. Static files only with index.html at the root. GET the event website for versions (version_number, created_at) and upload_limit_bytes. The web Publish card and Page tab also accept zip uploads and offer copyable error details.

Registration PUT accepts admit_pending: true with approval_required: false to admit waiting applicants atomically. Voting PUT requires confirm_vote_removal: true after confirmation when eligibility changes would remove earlier votes; otherwise 409 vote_removal_confirmation returns votes_to_remove. Website archive errors use invalid_archive, missing_index, blocked_file_type and site_too_large codes.

move the website's Overview button offers for the current stage. Moving the stage to results
also locks judging in the same step, when it was not locked already. Participants and judges
see the same stage pill and stage track as organisers, plus a separate scoring pill for judges.
A schedule that acts (2026-11-02): hack_get_content returns fixed_schedule beside schedule, the
event's real times as read-only rows marked fixed: true (event start and end, the entry deadline
or the caller's own team extension, the voting window, results published), each with set_in
naming where it changes. Never send them back. A schedule row's optional prompt (open, building,

entries. The cue only asks: the stage never moves by itself, so confirm with the organiser.
Teams (redesigned 2026-10-31): a team's creator is its first admin. Admins approve or decline
join requests, lock or unlock the team, rename it, edit its looking-for note, remove members,
make or remove other admins, and roll a new link, https://<hack host>/team/<code>, read with
hack_preview_team_link before joining. The last admin can't be unmade until someone else is
one, and the longest-standing remaining member takes over when an admin leaves. Locking clears
the team's pending requests and invites, and a locked team refuses every way in except
organiser placement. hack_create_team drops open, and hack_set_team_finding is gone, replaced

hack_new_my_team_link (organiser equivalents: hack_lock_team, hack_set_team_admin,
hack_new_team_link). hack_join_team's code takes a bare code or the whole link.

separate from locking. hack_list_open_teams reads every unlocked team (full flag included),
solo listings and pending offers. There is no "who can join" choice on a team any more, so a
former code-only team simply appears in this list too. Accepting or declining a request now
needs a team admin, invites stay any teammate's to send and the invitee's own to accept or
decline. hack_withdraw_team_request is unchanged. hack_remove_teammate is admin only and no
longer needs team finding on. Joining by any method clears other pending offers and the solo
listing, and leaving restores nothing. Organisers use hack_fill_teams with body.apply:false,
show the plan and confirm, then body.apply:true to place approved solo people into teams with
room, topped up to body.size (people per team, default 4), and new Team 1, Team 2 groups of
that size, avoiding name clashes and skipping locked teams. The apply plan uses current
membership. hack_update_event still accepts team_finding: off hides the lists and pending
offers and refuses new requests and invites, while codes, links, locking, admins and Fill
teams keep working either way.

After building a form, offer entry notifications through MCP Events or a dashboard webhook. Read the [notification reference](https://golden-host.invalid/docs/webhooks/) for signatures, retries, and limits. On Simple Host the same subscription also takes four site events, site.deployed, domain.status_changed, viewer.access_requested, and visitor.signed_up (visitor ID only, never an email, never the owner); Enterprise keeps the three record events, and Enterprise needs a separate port for the site events. On Simple Host, Web Push is a third notification kind on the same subscription (SIM-360, behind the account allowlist WEB_PUSH_ACCOUNTS, off until the owner enables it): the owner subscribes a browser device from the dashboard or `SH.push.subscribe()`, and a signed-in visitor may subscribe their own device too, site-wide or to one optional resource, to be told when the owner adds or edits their row. Not yet on Enterprise.
